claims.text: Elemental-subset variations in single-phase FCC alloys derived from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni modulate local short-range order.
Local short-range order affects dislocation mobility and slip-system activity.
Changes in dislocation mobility and slip-system activity govern differences in yield strength and ductility among these alloys.
Changing the elemental makeup alters the local chemical environment.
Changes in the local chemical environment affect the propensity for short-range-order formation.
Enhanced short-range order can create regions that pin or impede dislocations.
Short-range-order-mediated impediment of dislocation motion can elevate yield strength.
Enhanced short-range order can modify strain-hardening behavior.
Enhanced short-range order may reduce ductility.
Ternary or quaternary subsets that develop stronger short-range order than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni are expected to exhibit increased yield strength.
Ternary or quaternary subsets with stronger short-range order are expected to exhibit altered work-hardening behavior relative to the quinary baseline.
Subsets with reduced short-range order could have lower yield strength and different ductility than the quinary baseline.
Solid-solution strengthening may also contribute to mechanical-property differences among the alloys.
The proposed relationship is limited to single-phase FCC alloys under controlled thermomechanical processing and may fail where phase separation or grain-boundary effects dominate.
